entities.name: Doxycycline
observations: Bedtime dosing with recumbency can cause pill-induced esophagitis presenting with retrosternal burning and odynophagia.

entities.name: Pill-induced esophagitis
observations: Doxycycline-associated injury typically produces a discrete focal ulcer, often in the mid esophagus, with surrounding epithelial injury.
The clinical pattern is abrupt retrosternal pain or burning and odynophagia after medication exposure, especially with bedtime dosing or insufficient water.

entities.name: Mid-esophageal mirror ulcers
observations: Mirror-image or kissing ulcers surrounded by relatively normal mucosa are consistent with focal pill-induced esophageal injury.
